item.content:encoded:

🎙
President of Russia Vladimir Putin
chaired a meeting
of the Collective Security Council of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation in St Andrew’s Hall of the Grand Kremlin Palace
(Moscow, November 11, 2026)
A package of documents
was signed following the meeting, including
the Declaration of the CSTO Collective Security Council
.
💬
Vladimir Putin:
My colleagues and I have just held a thorough and productive exchange of views in
a restricted format
on
pressing global and regional security issues
.
We reached
full mutual understanding
on virtually every issue discussed. We reaffirmed our commitment to further joint efforts
to counter acute challenges and threats to collective security
.
I am pleased to note that Council members gave
a positive assessment of the results of
Russia’s CSTO chairmanship in 2026
. Our chairmanship benefited from
the friendly assistance and support
of our colleagues across the Organisation.
🤝
Together, we held more than a hundred events across key areas of cooperation.
We took coordinated steps to promote our common position on the international stage, including at the UN and other multilateral forums.
Our shared approaches
to the current situation in the world and our region, and
our vision of the priorities for the CSTO’s development
, are reflected in
the draft Declaration of the Collective Security Council
, which Russia has proposed adopting at today’s meeting.
As always, considerable attention was paid to improving the operational and combat readiness of the forces and assets within the collective security system
. A series of major joint exercises took place in Belarus, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and, of course, Russia. In particular,
the CSTO Collective Rapid Reaction Forces
successfully held
the Interaction 2026 exercise
in the Chelyabinsk Region alongside
the Centre-2026 strategic command post exercise
.
We also continued our systematic efforts to equip our collective forces with modern weapons and equipment.
I would like to stress that today we are to take
important decisions
on the further development of the CSTO Collective Forces. These concern, among other things, their
aviation component
and the formation of
mobile air defence units for joint military operations
.
Close operational contacts among our security agencies, law enforcement bodies and relevant services
helped strengthen coordination between our countries in combating terrorism, extremism, illicit drugs, drug trafficking and illegal migration. We also closely monitored
the situation in Afghanistan
as part of our efforts to strengthen security along the Organisation’s external borders.
Partnership among CSTO member states in
ensuring biological safety
and
countering the spread of dangerous infections
has gained considerable momentum.
☝️
Next year, 2027, will be particularly significant for our Organisation, marking two anniversaries:
35 years since the signing of
the Collective Security Treaty
and 25 years since
the establishment of the CSTO
.
Our friends in Tajikistan
, who will assume the chairmanship,
therefore face a substantial and demanding task
: both taking stock of our many years of cooperation and defining the strategic prospects for its further development.
Naturally, CSTO Member States will provide their colleagues in Tajikistan with
all the assistance they need
.

item.title: ☢️ Zaporozhskaya Nuclear Power Plant #ZNPP On November 11, an employee of the Zaporozhskaya NPP
item.description: ☢️ Zaporozhskaya Nuclear Power Plant ( #ZNPP ): On November 11, an employee of the Zaporozhskaya NPP was killed in his own home in a Ukrainian armed forces strike. The previous day, another of our colleagues – an electrical fitter at ZNPP – was killed on his way to work. The car he was travelling in was attacked by a Ukrainian drone. He died of his injuries at the scene. ◾️ This brings the number of plant employees killed since April 2026 to fifteen. The Ukrainian militants continue to strike residential buildings in Energodar and nearby villages. At night, while people sleep and recover before the next working day, their homes become targets. Living conditions in Energodar have a direct bearing on the safety of the ZNPP. Above all, the plant’s safety depends on its people. They need to be able to rest after their shifts and feel confident that their families are safe. ❗️ By continuing its strikes on the city’s nuclear workers and their homes, the Kiev regime is deliberately jeopardising nuclear safety. #KievRegimeCrimes

item.title: ⚔️ November 11 – the end of the Great Stand on the Ugra River – a memorable date in Russia's military history.
item.description: ⚔️ November 11 – the end of the Great Stand on the Ugra River – a memorable date in Russia's military history. #OTD in 1480 , after more than a month of confrontation on the banks of the Ugra River, Akhmat, Khan of the Great Horde, ordered his army to retreat. That spring, Khan Akhmat marched towards the Russian frontier with a large army, determined to reassert his authority by force. 🌊 At the mouth of the Ugra River, Akhmat found a Russian army waiting on the opposite bank . ⚔️
November 11 –
the end of
the Great Stand on the Ugra River
– a memorable date in Russia's military history.
#OTD
in 1480
, after more than a month of confrontation on the banks of the Ugra River,
Akhmat, Khan of the Great Horde, ordered his army to retreat.
His withdrawal marked
the end of the Tatar yoke
, which had lasted for more than two centuries, and ushered in
a new era for an independent Russian state
.
By 1480,
Grand Prince Ivan III of Moscow
had brought much of the Russian lands under his authority. By
ceasing to pay tribute to the Horde
, he had asserted the independence of Rus’. That spring,
Khan Akhmat
marched towards the Russian frontier with a large army, determined to reassert his authority by force.
🌊
At the mouth of the Ugra River, Akhmat found a Russian army waiting on the opposite bank
. Its commanders had secured the fords and other crossing points. On October 8, the Horde’s forces tried to cross, but the Russian warriors repelled them, and the two armies
settled into a standoff
that would last just over a month.
As the cold set in, Akhmat’s supplies ran low.
The reinforcements he expected from his Lithuanian allies never arrived. Meanwhile, detachments sent by Ivan III raided the Horde’s lightly defended rear.
🏳️
On November 11, 1480, Akhmat gave the order to retreat.
Thus, Rus’ had finally broken free of the yoke, without the pitched battle both sides had expected
. The Great Stand on the Ugra became a symbol of the rebirth of Russian sovereignty and of Moscow’s emergence as the country’s political and spiritual centre.

item.title: . On the passing of Alexander Darchiev, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America
item.description: On the passing of Alexander Darchiev, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America . The leadership and staff of the Russian Foreign Ministry announce with profound sorrow that Alexander Darchiev , Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the USA, passed away suddenly on November 11, aged 66. We have lost an outstanding diplomat, an experienced leader, a kind colleague and a mentor. An exceptional professional and a distinguished expert on the United States, Alexander Darchiev served in one of the most demanding areas of Russian foreign policy. We extend our deepest and most heartfelt condolences to Alexander Darchiev’s family and loved ones. The cherished memory of our colleague, taken from us far too soon, will remain in our hearts forever.

item.title: ⚡️ On the adoption by the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee of Russia’s resolution on combating the glorification of Nazism
item.description: ⚡️ On the adoption by the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee of Russia’s resolution on combating the glorification of Nazism On November 10 in New York, the Third Committee of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly adopted a resolution put forward by Russia entitled “Combating glorification of Nazism, neo-Nazism and other practices that contribute to fuelling contemporary forms of racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance” . 🌐 The resolution was co-sponsored by 45 states: Algeria, Angola, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, China, the Republic of the Congo, Cuba, the DPRK, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Guinea, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Lesotho, Mali, Namibia, Nicaragua, Niger, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Senegal, Serbia, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Togo, Turkmenistan, Uganda, Uzbekistan, Venezuela, Vietnam and Zimbabwe. ☝️ 117 states voted in favour , 53 voted against and nine abstained. The vote demonstrates the broad international support this key Russian initiative continues to enjoy at the UN. The resolution’s adoption is particularly significant this year . It marks 80 years since the International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg concluded the trial of senior officials of the Third Reich and 25 years since the World Conference against Racism adopted its outcome document, the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action

On November 10 in New York,
the Third Committee
of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly
adopted
a resolution put forward by Russia entitled
“Combating glorification of Nazism, neo-Nazism and other practices that contribute to fuelling contemporary forms of racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance”
.
🌐
The resolution was co-sponsored by 45 states:
Algeria, Angola, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, China, the Republic of the Congo, Cuba, the DPRK, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Guinea, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Lesotho, Mali, Namibia, Nicaragua, Niger, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Senegal, Serbia, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Togo, Turkmenistan, Uganda, Uzbekistan, Venezuela, Vietnam and Zimbabwe.
☝️
117 states voted in favour
, 53 voted against and nine abstained. The vote demonstrates
the broad international support
this key Russian initiative continues to enjoy at the UN.
The resolution’s adoption is particularly significant this year
. It marks
80 years
since
the International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg concluded the trial of senior officials of the Third Reich
and
25 years
since the World Conference against Racism adopted its outcome document,
the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action
.
The resolution expresses deep concern over any form of glorification
of the Nazi movement, neo-Nazism and former members of the Waffen-SS, including the erection of monuments and memorials and the holding of public demonstrations glorifying the Nazi past and neo-Nazism.
❗️
It is particularly alarming that
countries of the “collective West”
, especially EU member states, where these practices occur regularly,
refuse to acknowledge or address them and choose instead to oppose multilateral efforts to combat various forms of intolerance.
The stance taken by the former Axis powers
– Germany, Italy and Japan –
is of particular concern. T
heir votes against the resolution show that
they have forgotten the tragic lessons
of their own 20th-century history. They also cast doubt on the sincerity of their professed humanist values and their commitment to the obligations they assumed on joining the UN.
The resolution makes
a practical and substantial contribution to global efforts
to eradicate Nazism, racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and all forms of related intolerance.
🤝
Russia expresses its sincere gratitude to all those who stood firm on principle despite the pressure they faced
. They reaffirmed that any attempt to revise the outcome of World War II is unacceptable and that
the UN Charter
and
the Judgement of the Nuremberg Tribunal
remain
inviolable
.

item.title: 🎙 Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's answers to questions from the programme
item.description: 🎙 Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's answers to questions from the programme “Moscow. Kremlin. Putin” (Moscow, November 11, 2026) ❓ Question: How do you assess the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi? 💬 Sergey Lavrov: In this case, the trilateral format makes the most sense . As I understand it, the comments from all sides following the talks in Abu Dhabi were, overall, positive . I’m leaving Zelensky out of this. He’s always playing his own games. The negotiators themselves, though, seem to have been ready to get down to business . We’ll hear what Vladimir Medinskiy has to say when he returns with his delegation. ❓ Question: The Americans say they are coming to Moscow. A possible meeting between Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in China is just days away. Could the talks that have just concluded help lay the groundwork for discussions between the two Presidents? 💬 Sergey Lavrov: My understanding is that, as announced, the American negotiators are coming to Moscow to brief President Vladimir Putin. He will, of course, also receive a report from Vladimir Medinskiy’s delegation , as he regularly does. The President will decide how we proceed based on what he hears from the Americans. The course we take will be geared towards achieving the objectives of the special military operation . The President set out those objectives in June 2024 , and they have remained unchanged ever since.

item.title: ⚡️ On November 11, Moldova's Ambassador to Russia Lilian Darii was summoned to the Russian Foreign Ministry.
item.description: ⚡️ On November 11, Moldova's Ambassador to Russia Lilian Darii was summoned to the Russian Foreign Ministry. The Ministry issued a strong protest over the Moldovan authorities’ decision on October 23 to declare a staff member of the Russian Embassy in Chisinau persona non grata. The authorities cited as a pretext the alleged discovery of debris from a drone carrying explosives on Moldovan territory. The Ministry stressed that the lack of evidence that the drone was of Russian origin shows that the decision was based on a contrived pretext and constitutes yet another unfriendly act by Moldova. The move’s real aim is to further erode the centuries-old ties between Russia and Moldova and to obstruct the Russian diplomatic mission’s work in Chisinau at every turn. ❗️ The Moldovan Ambassador received a diplomatic note informing him that, in accordance with the principle of reciprocity , Russia has declared a staff member of the Moldovan Embassy in Russia persona non grata.

item.title: 🎙 Opening remarks by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at a meeting with Chairman of the Supervisory Board of the Serbian state-owned company Srbijagas
item.description: 🎙 Opening remarks by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at a meeting with Chairman of the Supervisory Board of the Serbian state-owned company Srbijagas Aleksandar Vulin (Moscow, November 11, 2026) 💬 Sergey Lavrov: We have known each other for a long time. We have also long known you as one of Serbia’s leading political figures. You have a keen understanding of political developments and always keep the Serbian people’s overriding goal in sight. Your work as Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Srbijagas also reflects our shared commitment to cooperation that benefits both our countries . Talks are currently under way on future gas supplies and a new long-term contract. I know that Director General of Srbijagas Dusan Bajatovic was also here. 🤝 We remain fully committed to all our agreements, past and present . We hope the new government, too, will ensure continuity in Serbia’s strategic partnership with the Russian Federation . I look forward to hearing your assessment of the latest developments in your country. #RussiaSerbia
